notes: Read SKILL.md and references/workflow-patterns.md in full. The skill teaches writing GitHub Actions workflows: triggers, matrix builds, job dependencies, environment protection, secrets/variables, caching, artifacts, Docker build-and-push, reusable workflows, self-hosted runners, debugging and permissions.

Mostly the output is YAML the agent writes into the user's .github/workflows; `run:` steps (npm, ./deploy.sh, aws s3 sync) execute in the user's CI with secrets referenced via ${{ secrets.* }}. Medium because the self-hosted runner section (SKILL.md:271-281) has the agent download a version-pinned runner tarball (v2.311.0) from github.com/actions/runner without a checksum, run its config.sh with a registration token, and start the runner on the user's machine. Acceptable because it is the official GitHub-documented setup path for a runner the user chose to host, pinned to a release, and requires the user's own registration token.

Review before adopting: the Debug step echoes `toJson(github)` (SKILL.md:305-308), which dumps the full event context to logs; the reusable-workflow caller pins to @main (references/workflow-patterns.md:9) and Docker pushes `user/app:latest`, contrary to the skill's own pinning advice (SKILL.md:333). Related Skills (SKILL.md:342-344) link to sibling skills ../gitlab-ci/, ../../containers/docker-management/ and ../../release/semantic-versioning/ as optional reading only.
